Your agent’s day

What would your agent actually do all day?

Pick the life closest to yours. Every add-on below is on the shelf today and included with Archie: nothing costs extra, and nothing here is a drawing of something we are planning.

Pick a life closest to yours

At work

At home

You bill by the hour, so the hour you lose chasing people is the one that costs twice.

  • SkillWaiting On Every reply you never got, and every invoice nobody paid.
  • SkillCommitment Keeper Reads your sent mail and pulls out every “I’ll send that over”.
  • SkillFind a Time Reads your calendar and drafts the reply that ends the back and forth.
  • RoutineFriday Week Check What moved this week, and what did not.

The same round of sign-ins, every month, before any of the actual work starts.

  • SkillStatement Collector Signs in to each account and downloads the month’s statement.
  • SkillClean Books Drop a statement PDF and it enters every charge.
  • SkillWaiting On The invoices that went out and never came back.
  • PersonalityThe Bookkeeper Numbers first. No lecture attached.

Half the day is deciding when, and the other half is getting there on time.

  • SkillFind a Time Say “find a time with Sam” and it drafts the reply.
  • SkillBooking Watch Who booked, what they typed in the form, who moved it.
  • SkillLeave Time When to walk out of the door, with today’s traffic in it.
  • SkillStay in Touch The past clients who quietly drift out of touch.

No front desk, so the admin lands between appointments or after them.

  • SkillBooking Watch Who booked, who moved it, who cancelled.
  • SkillCommon Questions Counts what people actually ask, and keeps one good agreed answer.
  • SkillMy Documents Straight answers out of your own lease, policy and paperwork.
  • SkillPaperwork Renewals with fourteen steps and no map: licenses, permits, registrations.

Customers waiting on an answer, and nobody whose job it is to sweep the inbox.

  • SkillOwed to Customers Sweeps the shared mail for anyone still waiting.
  • SkillLead Desk Every possible customer in one list, with the stage each has reached.
  • SkillRevenue Watch Reads your live Stripe: what failed, what is unpaid.
  • PersonalityThe Operator Runs on shifts, not calendar blocks.

Four schedules, one of them yours, and the school emails nobody has read.

  • SkillSchool & Family Pulls the dates, deadlines and what-to-bring out of the school mail.
  • SkillCalendar Manager “What does Tuesday look like?”, and the move it proposes before making it.
  • SkillBirthday & Anniversary Keeper Every date that matters, remembered early enough to act on.
  • SkillLeave Time When to actually leave, not when it starts.

Everything still has to happen, and you are doing it on four hours of sleep.

  • PersonalityNew Parent Written for one hand, at three in the morning.
  • SkillMedication & Refill Reminder What to take, the dose, and when the refill runs out.
  • SkillMeal Planner The week’s meals out of whatever is in the fridge.
  • SkillStay in Touch The people you meant to write back to three weeks ago.

You leave the appointment and half of what was said is already gone.

  • SkillHealth Record Tell it what the doctor said and it keeps the thread.
  • SkillMedication & Refill Reminder The list, the doses, and the refill dates.
  • SkillMy Documents Answers out of the policies and forms you were handed.
  • SkillPaperwork Benefits and enrollments, step by step, with the next one named.

Nothing here is hard. It is just that no one thing reminds you of any of it.

  • SkillHome Maintenance The jobs nobody remembers: furnace filters, drains, the gutters.
  • SkillWarranty & Returns When you bought it, and the day the return window shuts.
  • SkillPackage Tracker One live list, read out of your own shipping mail.
  • PersonalityHouse Manager Runs the house in weeks and seasons, not in hours.

You know roughly what comes in. What goes out is spread over eleven websites.

  • SkillBills & Subscriptions One list of everything that charges you on a repeat, with real dates.
  • SkillMoney In & Out Say what you spent as you go, then ask how much is left.
  • SkillSavings Goals Name what you are saving for, and ask whether you are on track.
  • RoutineBill Reminders Before the charge, not after it.

Nine applications in, and the spreadsheet tracking them is already out of date.

  • SkillJob Hunt Every application in one list, moved along by the confirmation mail itself.
  • SkillThe Right Words Paste the message, get replies you can actually send.
  • SkillCircle Back You mention Thursday’s interview; on Friday it asks how it went.
  • RoutineApplication Sweep What has gone quiet, and who is worth a nudge.

The reading is done. Whether any of it stuck is a different question.

  • SkillCourse Companion Turns the lectures and the syllabus into something you know.
  • SkillLearning Coach Explains it, makes the flashcards, and remembers where you struggled.
  • RoutineDaily Study Review A few minutes on what you are closest to forgetting.
  • PersonalityStudy Partner Explains it until it actually clicks.

Four out of 160 each time, and the pick changes nothing about what your agent may do on its own. A draft waits for you to send it. A calendar change is proposed, then applied after you approve it. It cannot spend money or buy anything. The whole list, and how to check it →

Your agent’s thinking goes to the AI company you picked, on your own account. If your work carries a confidentiality rule, that is the sentence to hold it against, and everything that leaves your computer is written out line by line.

None of these is quite you.

Most people are two of them at once, and your agent holds as many add-ons as you hand it. If the job you have in mind is not on the shelf, say what you wish your agent could do and it writes the skill.
